# Recoloring structural grid dividers

Use this pattern when a grid has a background color, repeated full-width horizontal bands, and a full-height vertical band (or narrow stripe) in another color. The same divider color may also appear as isolated marks/noise.

## Procedure
1. Inspect the grid for rows that are entirely one foreground color and columns (or a narrow contiguous group of columns) that repeat that color across most/all rows. Treat the intersection network as structural dividers.
2. Use a demonstration output to identify the replacement color for those dividers. In the observed example, the full-row and full-height divider pixels changed to a new color, while isolated same-colored marks remained unchanged.
3. Apply the recolor only to the structural divider rows/columns. Preserve the background and incidental marks, including marks of the original divider color that are outside the structural lines.
4. Check intersections and dimensions carefully; horizontal divider rows and vertical divider columns should all use the replacement color, yielding consistent full bands.

## Caution
Do not globally replace every pixel of the divider's original color. Distinguish the repeated line structure from isolated objects/noise, and infer the target color from demonstrations rather than assuming a fixed color mapping.",

# Recolor structural dividers, not isolated marks

For an ARC grid with a background color, repeated full-width horizontal bands, and a full-height vertical stripe, identify the divider network and recolor only its pixels. Demonstrations may show the target replacement color.

## Procedure
1. Find rows that consist entirely of one non-background color and columns (or a contiguous stripe of columns) consistently carrying that color across the grid. These are structural separators.
2. Use the demonstration pair to infer the new color for those separator cells. Do not assume a fixed palette mapping.
3. Recolor the full horizontal and vertical separators, including their intersections, to the inferred target color.
4. Preserve all off-separator cells, including isolated cells of the original separator color that may be noise or objects. Do not globally replace the original color.
5. Verify row/column indices and preserve dimensions.

## Demonstrated pattern
In one example, color 6 formed two full horizontal rows and a two-column vertical stripe over a color-8 background. Those separator cells became color 2, but scattered color-6 cells outside the separator network remained color 6. Apply the same structural reasoning when palette/grid dimensions differ.",
